title: The Fox and the Crow
text:
A crow found a piece of cheese, or in older versions a piece of meat, and flew up to a branch to eat it in peace. A fox passing below caught the smell and stopped. He wanted that cheese, and he knew he could not climb the tree to take it.

So he looked up admiringly. "What a beautiful bird," he said. "Such glossy feathers, such a graceful neck, such bright eyes. Surely a bird so handsome must also have a lovely voice. If only I could hear you sing just once, I would know you were the queen of all the birds."

The crow was delighted. Nobody had ever praised her like that, and she wanted to prove the fox right. She lifted her head, opened her beak wide and gave her loudest caw.

The cheese fell straight down. The fox snapped it up before it touched the ground. "Your voice is fine," he said as he trotted away. "What you are missing is sense."
lesson: When someone praises you lavishly, ask what they want from you. Enjoy sincere compliments, but do not let flattery make your decisions.
source: Aesop's Fables (Perry Index 124); La Fontaine, Fables I.2
